newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco earnings hinge on price increases-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco earnings hinge on price increases-analysts.

text.p: Tobacco companies' long-term earnings outlook depends on how much they are able to raise cigarette prices in the wake of the proposed litigation settlement reached last week between the industry and state attorneys general.
"There are a lot of variables," said K. Timothy Swanson, an analyst at A.G. Edwards. "But the big unknown is what effect the higher prices will have on demand."
The companies are almost sure to raise cigarette prices to try to cover the cost of the settlement, estimated at $368.5 billion over 25 years, analysts said.

While it still unclear whether those increases will ultimately cut into long-term earnings by reducing demand, analysts are certain that 1998 earnings will show a sharp drop. That is because of the initial $10.5 billion payout the companies would make as part of the settlement, as well as the interest on that amount.

Philip Morris Cos Inc, which according to some reports is expected to make an initial $6.5 billion payout, would trim about $0.40 a share maximum from 1998 earnings as a result, said Allan Kaplan, an analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Kaplan, who said Philip Morris would finance the payment by taking on debt, lowered his 1998 earnings estimate for the company to between $3.00 and $3.20 a share, from $3.42.
Philip Morris officials were not immediately available to comment. The company's board said in a late afternoon statement that it supported the settlement.

R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, said in an Securities and Exchange Commission filing it would initially pay about $600 million. Including interest payments, that translates into about an impact on earnings of $0.49 per share in 1998, according to Roy Burry, an analyst at Oppenheimer & Co.
Burry estimated the company would earn about $2.98 a share for that year.
David Adelman, an analyst at Morgan Stanley, said RJR would likely spin off the remaining 80.0 percent of its food business to help defer the costs of the payout.
After such a spin-off, the company would earn about $1.40 a share for 1998, Adelman said, down from his previous estimate of $2.00.
RJR Reynolds officials were not immediately available to comment.
Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett tobacco unit would likely go bankrupt as a result of the settlement, a person close to the company told Reuters.
UST Inc, Loews Corp and Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc are among other tobacco companies that the settlement would also affect.
